notes: Every category level in the portal menu, and a new group stays open

entries.title: Every category level in the portal menu, and a new group stays open
items: The portal's header menu shows every level of categories under a parent, indented — not just the first. Sub-category tiles list what sits under each one, and an empty category lists its sub-categories instead of stopping at Nothing here yet.
Creating a user group keeps it open on its editor, ready for its catalog, limits and rules — no Edit click.
A test world's portal developer page (/p/…/api) loads its reference for staff previewing it or signed in as one of its people.

entries.title: Empty categories show in the portal
items: A category shows in the portal's menu before any product is in it, so a brand set up with its categories first sees the whole structure from day one. Opening an empty one says Nothing here yet.
User groups still decide: a group limited to Only these categories sees just those, everything under them, and the parents that lead to them.

entries.title: Add many SKUs to a category, and categories you can tell apart
items: Each category has a SKUs tab: In category and Not in category, with search and sortable columns. Tick SKUs (or every one the search shows) and press Add to category or Remove from category. Other categories shows where each SKU already sits.

A SKU's Categories box is now the tree: each top-level category in its own box with its sub-categories under it, so two called Sale under different parents can't be mixed up. The SKU's categories are listed above as full paths, and a Find box narrows a long list.
In the portal, People is now Users — the menu, the page and the help.
On a SKU, Customs value is now Fair market value — the declared value per unit for international shipments.

entries.title: Nothing being made: cancelled jobs under waiting orders
items: A cancelled print piece is never printed again on its own — before, the next change to its order quietly made a new one. If the order still wants it, the Print queue and the order page show “LUMI-000123 still needs 250 × NSF-BC and nothing is being made”, with Make a new job, or take the item off the order.
The same for kits: a cancelled work order under a waiting order shows under Nothing being built on the Kitting page, counting kits being built ahead for stock.
A print piece that is queued, in QC or out for a proof no longer gets a duplicate job when its order is edited.

entries.title: Taking items off orders, packing after picking, and rush per SKU
items: Fix order → Remove asks first and shows what is credited: the units, and the pick fee if nobody picked it. Picked or already printed? Tick “Also credit the work already done” to credit the pick fee, print setup and per-piece printing at the rate billed — stocked and print-on-demand items alike.
Brands can take an item off their own order in the portal (order page → Remove from order) while nothing is picked and it isn't being printed. Its fees are credited.
Packing always starts from picking: an order nobody picked can't be packed. Print-on-demand items go straight to the bench once they're marked printed.

SKU → Pricing & limits → Rush orders: let a SKU be rushed or not, with the reason buyers see (“it ships by freight only”). Checkout greys out rush with that reason, and rush orders, sooner ship dates and switching to rush are refused the same way.
Settings → Shipping → Print on demand: shipping days to print and ship for print SKUs without their own Ships within, and whether print on demand can be rushed (off unless ticked).

entries.title: HP Site Flow: connect and check
items: Settings → Integrations → HP Site Flow: connect Live or Stage with the API token and secret (stored encrypted) and the destination account. Connect & check confirms the credentials without creating anything.

Check a print piece: type its number and see the exact Site Flow order it would become — product code, quantity, print file, shipment — with Site Flow's own verdict. Nothing is sent yet; sending and status back come next.

entries.title: Clearer answers on the floor
items: Finish pressed twice (or after the other picker finished) says the order is already finished, and the pick screen counts it as done. Confirm shipped pressed again shows shipped, not an error.
Picking an order that was just cancelled says so, and lists what to put back and where. Cancel order now asks first.

Scanning the wrong lot names the lot the order is reserved; a late answer for a wrong-location scan no longer overwrites the stop you've moved on to; a label read twice into the count no longer confirms it.
Moving from a location whose stock is on license plates names the plates to scan. A cart can be reopened by its batch number after a refresh or a rebooted gun.
A retry after a crashed server process is no longer stuck on "still being worked on" for two minutes.

entries.title: Stock stays right when two people collide
items: Undoing a receipt takes the units back from where they were moved, not from the biggest pile of that product.

Two receivers making the same new lot at once both succeed; l26002 and L26002 (or a copy-pasted code with hidden characters) are one lot; a lot with a different expiry than the one on file is refused with both dates; receiving an already-expired lot warns.
A pallet moved from a page that was out of date is told where it went instead of moving it twice; a pick-face refill can't be done twice; a double-tapped bench pull books once.

Counts: blind counts stay blind over the API, two counters on one line can't overwrite each other, a count can't be cancelled once part of it is in the ledger, and a location that doesn't exist is named.

The kitting bench and print pull parts and blanks that receiving put on license plates; a print job started twice pulls its blanks once; a truck can be received onto the dock while its SKU is being counted.
Sanity limits: adjustments, counts, order lines and import numbers can't be absurd (a million at most, hex and 1e20 refused).

entries.title: Imports that say what's wrong
items: An unclosed quote, or the same column twice in the header, is refused with the line it's on — before anything is written. Errors name the line as your spreadsheet shows it, blank rows counted.
A file that repeats the same row is flagged before it's imported. Files up to 25 MB reach the import (bigger ones are told so), and Excel files can't unpack to more than 128 MB.
Location codes are checked (letters, digits and - _ . /, up to 32, never a formula); a trading partner's licence date must be a date.

entries.title: Reports: order details, backorders, tracking — and who gets them
items: Portal reports: Order summary (one row per order, as before), Order details (every item: ordered, shipped, still owed), Backorders (what's waiting on stock) and Tracking (shipped orders with carrier and tracking).
Order details and Backorders filter by item, category (everything under it), item type, and kits — on screen, in the CSV, and in scheduled emails.
A report built for a brand can be given to particular people and user groups, not just roles.
The report builder has Item type and Categories on every product report.

entries.title: Custom SKU fields and item type
items: Each brand can have its own SKU fields — Customer → SKUs → Fields: Propago's Custom 01–05 or named ones — each shown to buyers or kept for the warehouse and billing.
Item type on every SKU (Brochure, Apparel…), filterable in reports. Propago's item type and Custom 01–05 come over with new SKUs.

entries.title: Update SKUs in bulk from a spreadsheet
items: The SKU import now updates the brand's existing SKUs too, changing only the cells you fill in: a sheet of just sku and price updates prices. Export CSV from the SKU list, edit it, import it back.

entries.title: A removed line gives back its pick fee
items: Removing a line from an order before anyone picked it now credits its pick fee, as its unit fee already was — the client is no longer billed a pick that never happened. A line removed after it was picked keeps its fee: the pick was done.

entries.title: A calendar for each brand, with reminders
items: Brands put their big dates on a calendar — a launch, a trade show, Paris Fashion Week — from the portal's account menu → Calendar. Staff can add them too, under the customer → Calendar.
It opens as a month grid with each event across the days it runs (Prev, Next, Today); click a day to add an event there, or switch to List for the dates soonest first.

Pick when to be reminded (30 days, 2 weeks, 1 week, the day before, on the day). On those days the brand's admins, whoever added it and any extra addresses get an email and a note on the bell; in the warehouse, the teams that chose "Client event coming up" (Settings → Teams) and the brand's account manager are told.
Settings → Teams now also lists the Billing events, which were missing from the list.

entries.title: Two low-stock lines: an early warning, then the alert
items: A SKU can have an Early warning level above its low-stock alert (Pricing & limits → Commerce). Set 100 and 50: the brand hears "Getting low (early warning)" at 100, then "Just went low" at 50.
Propago's second reorder minimum comes over as the early warning; the SKU import takes a low_stock_warning column.

entries.title: Approval thresholds per product, per user group
items: New in a SKU's Commerce section: Approval threshold. Orders above so many units of this product wait for approval — one number for everyone, and a different one for any user group (above 5 for most buyers, above 10 for Marketing).
A group's own threshold now replaces the everyone one for its people, for any ordering limit of the same kind — before, both applied.

entries.title: Allowances for the whole group, by calendar month
items: A user group's allowances can be shared by the whole group — "this group, 3 orders a month" — as well as for each person.
Allowances can run per calendar month, quarter or year, besides lifetime and rolling days. The shop and the person's page say which ("this month, shared by the group").

entries.title: A brand's own portal roles, and power buyers
items: Customer → Client portal → Roles: add the brand's own roles — Field rep, Marketing, Finance — each built on buyer, approver or brand admin, with eleven switches for whose orders they see and approve, placing orders, people, addresses, accounting units, reports, inbound, and skipping approvals or limits.
Pick the brand's roles for people on People, staff side or in the portal. Editing a role changes its people at once; deleting one puts them back on its base role.
Power buyer, on a person: their orders skip approvals and ordering limits, whatever their role. Stock, minimums and pack multiples still apply.

entries.title: Kits get their own page
items: A customer's Catalog menu now has Categories, SKUs and Kits. Kits lists the products built from other SKUs, with New kit; the SKU list keeps everything else, kit parts included.
The design studio's "Catalog page" step is now "Shop page", the name buyers see on the portal.

entries.title: User groups: a category tree, and products one by one
items: "Only these categories" shows every level as a tree. Tick a category and everything under it comes with it — its sub-categories show as "included". Before, a ticked parent didn't bring its sub-categories' products.
New on a group's Catalog tab: Products, one by one. Find a product and choose Always show (an extra SKU this group wouldn't otherwise see) or Always hide.

entries.title: The same category name under two parents
items: Skincare > Sale and Gifts > Sale can now both exist — a name only has to be unique among the categories beside it. Adding a second "Sale" under the same parent says so plainly.
The SKU import's categories column takes paths: "Makeup > Lipsticks" files the product there, making any level that's missing.
The reorganizer's spreadsheet writes each category as its path, and reads paths back, so two categories with the same name never get mixed up.

entries.title: Security update
items: A library Amphora uses to check what's sent to it is updated, closing a way an oversized request could use up the server's memory. Nothing changes on screen.

entries.title: Categories at every level, and a merge that keeps user groups
items: The Categories card shows the whole tree — sub-categories of sub-categories included. Before, anything deeper than two levels was hidden from the card even though it existed.
Add a sub-category straight from the card: pick where it goes (Top level, or Under a category) next to the name, then Add.

Reorganize the catalog checks each change the moment you add it, so Apply is always one click ("Apply 2 changes"). Reshape the tree nests at any depth — drop a category onto another to put it under that one.

Merging a category into one of its own sub-categories now works: the kept one takes its place. User groups limited to "Only these categories", and their allowances, follow a merge or delete too, and Undo puts them back.
"view SKUs" and each category's SKU count open this customer's own SKU list, filtered to that category and everything under it. The SKU list has a category filter of its own.

entries.title: The design studio previews every setting before you publish
items: Featured products, the Orders page's opening tab, related products, low-stock-first, labels on the reports, accounting and bulk pages, and the approvals ship-to all change in the preview as you set them. Before, these only showed after Publish.
Buyers still see the published portal until you press Publish. The draft is yours alone — another designer previewing the same portal sees their own.

entries.title: The menu stays where you left it
items: Clicking an item low in the side menu no longer throws the menu back to the top: the menu stays put while the page scrolls, and so does a customer's own menu.
Fold any menu group you don't use by clicking its heading. This device remembers what you folded; the group holding the page you're on always stays open.

entries.title: Pick runs walk pick priority 1 first
items: The pick slip and the scan station now send pickers to locations in pick-priority order — priority 1, then 2, then 3 — before anything without a priority, which follows the walk path as before. Amphora already took the right quantities from each location; it listed the stops in walk order, so a priority-3 shelf could come first on the slip.
The slip's ROUTE line now reads "pick priority first, then walk-path order".

entries.title: Find a location by typing it when receiving a pallet
items: Location on the Receive desk's Pallet mode is now a search box: type or scan part of a code and the list narrows to match. Leave it blank to land the pallet on the dock, as before.
Location lists everywhere are in aisle order — MAIN46-B-6-5 now comes before MAIN46-B-46-1 instead of after it.

entries.title: Portal typefaces ship with Amphora
items: The typefaces a portal theme can choose now come inside Amphora itself instead of being fetched from Google when Amphora is built — nothing changes on screen, and portals never load fonts from Google.

entries.title: Security update
items: Amphora now runs on a patched version of its web framework, closing a critical issue in image handling and a way to slow the server down. Nothing changes on screen; update when you can.
